title: Tokenizer & Context Concordance: Ops Runbook and Auto-Validation Pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description: Maintain and automate the compatibility inventory between primary models and their fallback variants to ensure tokenizer behavior, KV cache context boundaries, and operator tooling remain consistent across routing tiers and regions.
background: Smart routing increasingly relies on falling back to cheaper or regional variants when capacity or latency targets are breached.
Several recent incidents surfaced subtle tokenizer/context mismatches that caused token-count drift and degraded prompt semantics during fallbacks.
We need an operational runbook plus an automated CI validation pipeline to detect and remediate divergence before rollouts and to monitor drift post-deploy.
technical_plan: Inventory: canonical CSV mapping source-model -> fallback-model -> tokenizer-version -> kv-context-format -> supported-tools (sampler, scorer, trace hooks).
Schema: add lightweight manifest validation (manifest.json) to each variant bundle with tokenizer hash, vocab size, context-schema-id, and supported tool versions.
Auto-check: implement CI job 'compat-check' that pulls manifests for a change in model registry and runs tokenization equivalence tests over a curated prompt set (small/edge/long-tail).
Runtime hook: add a compatibility-gating middleware in routing that asserts manifest compatibility at request-time and emits a metric if mismatch is seen, without blocking traffic (initially).
Repair flow: on incompatibility detection, create a remediation PR template and enqueue supportive tasks (tokenizer upgrade, adaptor mappings, or fallthrough policy update).
Observability: dashboard with per-model pair mismatch rate, average token delta, and recent failing prompt examples stored for triage.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable manifest exists for every model variant in the model catalog and is fetched by the CI job without manual configuration.
CI job 'compat-check' runs in <10 minutes for a delta and fails the PR if tokenization equivalence is outside agreed tolerance for >5% of the curated prompts.
Routing middleware logs a compatibility metric and attaches example prompts when a runtime mismatch occurs; metric visible on the compatibility dashboard.
Runbook documented (confluence link below) with clear remediation steps and the maintenance owner identified.
At least one automatic remediation path exists for simple tokenizer drift (vocab patch or mapping) and a checklist for manual actions for complex cases.
outcome_metrics: PR_block_rate_due_to compat-check failures (initially should be >0 until fixed)
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from tolerance thresholds: mitigate by running CI in permissive mode for two cycles and tuning thresholds using historical drift data.
Increased CI runtime: mitigate by using a small representative prompt corpus and selective sampling for frequent model changes.
Runtime overhead from middleware: mitigate by sampling requests (1%) for live checks and increasing sampling only after confidence.
Manifest divergence due to human error: mitigate by adding registry webhooks and a lightweight preflight validator in the model packaging pipeline.
implementation_steps: Step 1 (Wk1): Define manifest schema and publish spec to confluence; small RFC to infra-team.
Step 2 (Wk2): Implement manifest generation in model-build pipeline and add to artifact storage.
Step 3 (Wk3): Build compat-check CI job and wire to model-registry webhooks and runtime PRs.
Step 4 (Wk4): Add routing middleware metric emission and create dashboard widgets.
Step 5 (Wk5): Pilot gating in canary region and run permissive CI for two cycles, tune thresholds, then promote to blocking mode.
Step 6: Create runbook and schedule knowledge transfer with SRE and platform teams.
Step 7: Automate simple remediation PRs for tokenizer mapping patches (follow-up epic).
